faq.q: Is EPS mandatory for all employees?
faq.a: Yes, if you are an employee whose basic salary plus dearness allowance is up to ₹15,000 per month, and you are covered under the EPF Act, then membership to EPS is mandatory. For those earning above ₹15,000, EPF is mandatory, and consequently, EPS also applies, although the contribution is capped at the ₹15,000 wage ceiling.

faq.q: Can I contribute more to EPS?
faq.a: No, the contribution to EPS is fixed at 8.33% of the employer's share of EPF contribution, calculated on a maximum wage ceiling of ₹15,000 per month. There is no provision for an employee to voluntarily contribute more to EPS.

faq.q: What happens if I change jobs?
faq.a: If you change jobs, your pensionable service can be transferred from your old EPF account to your new one. If your service is less than 10 years, you should obtain a Scheme Certificate to carry forward your service period. If you have completed 10 or more years, your pensionable service is already recorded, and you will be eligible for a pension at retirement.

faq.q: What is the minimum pension under EPS?
faq.a: The Central Government has a provision for a minimum pension of ₹1,000 per month for EPS pensioners, subject to certain conditions and notifications. This ensures a basic income for even those with minimal contributions or service.

Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) who were EPF members while working in India and met the eligibility criteria (e.g., 10 years of service) can claim EPS benefits upon retirement, provided they follow the due process and submit the necessary documents to EPFO.

Yes, the monthly pension received under the Employee Pension Scheme (EPS) is considered taxable income under the head "Income from other sources" and is subject to income tax as per the applicable slab rates.

A Scheme Certificate is a document issued by the EPFO to members who have completed less than 10 years of pensionable service. It records the member's service period and allows them to carry forward this service to a new employer, enabling them to accumulate the minimum 10 years required for a monthly pension.
